youtube.title: strata — a memory rebuilt, in three modes | 15 min dark ambient
youtube.description:
Dark ambient ritual music: a 15-minute piece in D minor at 76 BPM for kalimba, timpani, frame drums, bowed strings and drone, where one three-note refrain is buried and recovered over three movements.

The refrain is the memory. It opens as three notes on a kalimba (root, sixth, octave), is lost, and is rebuilt a note at a time until the whole line plays in every voice at once, and then alone. The notes on the page never change: the two degrees the modes move under them do the work, so the same line reads grave in D aeolian (wood), a semitone darker in D phrygian (stone) and warm in D dorian (air).

Three strata, one ground. 294 bars, 24 sections, written as text and rendered in the browser.

Chapters
0:00 Dust — the refrain, three notes on a kalimba
0:25 Wood — the first stratum, D aeolian
2:18 Carry
4:25 Stone — the second stratum, D phrygian
6:31 Forge
8:00 Strain
8:37 Shatter
9:28 Ash — the rebuild begins
10:56 Gather — the third stratum, D dorian
12:37 Whole — the line in every voice at once
13:53 After
14:56 Dust again

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/strata.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/

prompt: a 17-minute ritual epic: a memory (the refrain) rebuilt across three movements in D aeolian, phrygian and dorian, ending where it began
